assertion.rationale: CORRECTION (Task 23 register reconciliation): the #f5 and #f11 evidence anchors were each removed from this array the moment the commit that closed them landed (9f49c82 dropped #f5; 385b862 dropped #f11), leaving only #f12 even though this file's own rationale below still says 'F5, F11 and F12 -- the only three findings ... that cite 3.14.1 -- are all CLOSED.' That is a register asserting three contributors in prose while citing one in evidence -- restored to three rather than left self-contradictory. F5 was already CLOSED (Task 3, see 3.12.3) before this control's F11 update: the dead node --check glob step in lint-ci.yml was deleted rather than patched, restoring npm test across all 7 workspaces to the required-checks gate. F11 is CLOSED (Task 14): Action.OpenUrl.url and Image.url in AdaptiveCardView.tsx are constrained by an /^https?:\/\//i allowlist (rejects javascript:, case-varied and whitespace-padded variants, data:, vbscript:; the fallback UnsupportedElement renders instead of a dropped/blank element), both nginx templates now emit a Content-Security-Policy (script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline', required because Fluent UI v9's Griffel injects CSS-in-JS with no nonce wired up; connect-src scoped to Direct Line's REST+websocket host, the directline-token Function's default hostname, and the Application Insights Web SDK's config/ingestion hosts — verified in a real browser against the built bundle) plus X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy, and both frontend Dockerfiles now drop to USER nginx. F12 is now CLOSED (Task 15): scrubSql (apps/mcp-tools/src/tools/sql-dialect.ts) returns { text, terminated } instead of a bare string, and assertReadOnlySingleStatement rejects with an 'unterminated comment or quoted section' message BEFORE the single-statement check, the forbidden-verb check or the SELECT/WITH check run — so a partially-scrubbed scan result is never trusted by anything downstream. Block-comment nesting is now dialect-aware: depth is tracked only when dialect === 'tsql' (T-SQL genuinely nests, so a crafted `/* a /* b */` with one real close must stay open); for 'sqlite' the first `*/` closes, matching the real engine, which does not nest. Verified against the exact reproduction in F12: `SELECT 1 /* a /* b */ ; DELETE FROM launches` against 'tsql' now throws 'unterminated' (the comment genuinely never closes under T-SQL rules); the same text against 'sqlite' is correctly seen as a CLOSED comment (first */ wins) that exposes ' ; DELETE FROM launches' as a live second statement, which the pre-existing single-statement check now catches because it is no longer hidden by over-scrubbing; an unterminated backtick, quote or bracket is rejected the same way in both dialects. A legitimate non-nesting comment (`/* note: a/b ratio */`) still passes in both dialects, and all 27 pre-existing bypass probes (stacked statements, schema columns containing keyword substrings, string-literal contents, comment-smuggled verbs, WAITFOR, sp_/xp_ prefixes, SQLite file/schema escapes) still behave correctly — apps/mcp-tools test count moved from 277 to 287 (root suite: 858 -> 868, exit 0). ADDENDUM (2026-08-28, post-publication): the sentence that stood here said F5, F11 and F12 were "the only three findings ... that cite 3.14.1". That stopped being true the day F37 and F38 were raised, and a register that narrates its own contributor list has to keep it current or stop making the claim. FIVE findings now cite 3.14.1, and all five are CLOSED. F37: the data-api container image built, pushed and passed a clean Trivy scan, and could not start -- its runtime stage copied only /repo/node_modules while five non-dev packages (an exact pin of @azure/monitor-opentelemetry-exporter and four @opentelemetry packages it drags with it) resolve into apps/data-api/node_modules, which nothing copied. Both trees are now copied and Node resolves the nested one first, and the pin that caused the nesting moved to beta.44 -- which also removed the one @opentelemetry/core copy in the tree below 2.8.0 (open Dependabot alert CVE-2026-54285, unbounded memory allocation in W3C Baggage propagation, runtime scope), a package the Dockerfile fix on its own would have shipped into the image. F38: three shipped images were FROM nginx:1.27-alpine, a tag Docker Hub last rebuilt on 2025-04-16 because 1.27 is an end-of-line release, so sixteen months of Alpine security updates were absent from them; the pin moved to 1.31-alpine and .github/dependabot.yml gained the docker ecosystem it had never had, which is what stops the next pin rotting unseen. Neither finding was reachable by reading the repository, and neither was found by an audit pass: F37 came from F22's container smoke test and F38 from F33's repinned Trivy gate, both on their first real execution. The flaw-remediation claim this control makes is therefore stronger than it was on 2026-08-27, not weaker -- two flaws were identified and corrected by the repository's own mechanisms rather than by inspection.

recommendation: None outstanding for this control. (Deleting lint-ci's dead node-test step, Task 3/3.12.3; the Adaptive Card URL allowlist, CSP and non-root nginx user, Task 14; and the dialect-aware structural-validity check in the SQL gate, Task 15, are all DONE.) A regression here — the lint-ci node leg reintroduced and silently broken again, an unguarded Action/element url or a CSP relaxation, or scrubSql's nesting reverted to dialect-blind — would reopen this control. ADDENDUM (2026-08-28): also DONE for F37 (apps/data-api/Dockerfile copies both dependency trees) and F38 (nginx pinned to 1.31-alpine; docker ecosystem added to .github/dependabot.yml). A regression in either -- the nested workspace node_modules dropped from the image again, or a base-image pin left to go end-of-line unwatched -- would reopen this control.
